$description: #236-R1 source register. One row per source FAMILY. Every url_fetched was fetched by this lane on 2026-09-02; quotes are <=15-word receipts. Shaped for a generator: stable id, kind, licence, caution.

families.name: Laws of UX
families.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 — link on page: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/ ; footer "Laws of UX © Jon Yablonski 2026"
families.quote: Laws of UX © Jon Yablonski 2026 Contact | Privacy | License
families.relevance: Dave's source 1; the popular index the brain must exceed, not copy — ND licence forbids derivatives.
families.caution: SECONDARY. Every item here needs its primary study found separately; it is an index, not evidence.

families.name: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics
families.licence: "Copyright © 1998-2026 Nielsen Norman Group, All Rights Reserved" (quoted from the NN/g F-pattern page footer)
families.quote: 1: Visibility of System Status 2: Match Between the System and the Real World
families.relevance: The default review vocabulary for any screen the factory outputs; candidate C-tier rubric spine.

families.name: Shneiderman's Eight Golden Rules of Interface Design
families.licence: UNPROVEN: no licence statement in fetched text
families.quote: These principles, derived from experience and refined over three decades, require validation and tuning
families.relevance: Self-graded by its own author as needing validation — the cleanest example of a C-tier source admitting its tier.

families.name: Tognazzini's First Principles of Interaction Design
families.licence: page carries a "release for you to copy this post" style notice (quoted fragment; full terms not parsed)
families.quote: The following principles are fundamental to the design and implementation of effective interfaces
families.relevance: Contains Latency Reduction, Defaults, Protect Users' Work — three areas Apollo already rules by eye.

families.name: GOV.UK Government Design Principles
families.licence: Open Government Licence v3 (quoted from page)
families.quote: 1. Start with user needs 2. Do less 3. Design with data 4. Do the hard work to make it simple
families.relevance: 'Be consistent, not uniform' (#9) is the closest public statement of Apollo's four-theme problem.

families.name: ISO 9241 series (ergonomics of human-system interaction)
families.item_count: 7 interaction principles (110) + usability definition (11) + HCD process (210)
families.licence: ISO copyright, paywalled — only the abstract page was fetched
families.quote: ISO 9241-110:2020 Ergonomics of human-system interaction — Part 110: Interaction principles
families.relevance: The only ISO-blessed principle set; titles and dates PROVEN, the seven principle names are NOT (see UNPROVEN).
families.caution: Titles/dates fetched. The 7 principle names are behind the paywall — do not enter them into the KG from memory.

families.name: WCAG 2.2
families.licence: W3C Document Licence (page carries a Copyright section; W3C standard terms)
families.quote: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels
families.relevance: s234-D3 already binds the factory to WCAG 2.2 AA + 2.4.10 / 2.5.5 / 2.4.13; s116-D1 cites 2.5.8 for data marks.

families.name: EN 301 549 V3.2.1
families.quote: EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (2021-03) HARMONISED EUROPEAN STANDARD Accessibility requirements for ICT
families.relevance: The procurement standard a bank's suppliers are measured against; wraps WCAG and adds non-web ICT clauses.

families.name: European Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882)
families.licence: EU reuse policy (not quoted from page)
families.quote: The Directive on the accessibility requirements for products and services
families.relevance: In application from 28 June 2025 for consumer banking services — the hard floor under every Apollo screen shipped in the EU.
families.caution: The 28-June-2025 application date was NOT found in the fetched text: see UNPROVEN.

families.name: FCA Consumer Duty (PRIN 2A)
families.quote: product governance, price and value, consumer understanding and supporting consumers
families.relevance: THE regulator for Dave's clients. 'Consumer understanding' is a legal duty that lands directly on copy, hierarchy and disclosure design.

families.name: Digital Services Act Article 25 (dark-pattern prohibition)
families.licence: UNPROVEN: mirror site, no licence statement fetched
families.quote: shall not design, organise or operate their online interfaces in a way that deceives or manipulates
families.relevance: Turns a chunk of the persuasion literature into ILLEGAL, not merely unethical. The single strongest reason the brain must carry grade L.
families.caution: Fetched from a mirror; EUR-Lex returned HTTP 202 with 0 bytes to this agent. See UNPROVEN.

families.name: EDPB Guidelines 03/2022 on deceptive design patterns
families.quote: Guidelines 03/2022 on deceptive design patterns in social media platform interfaces
families.relevance: The GDPR-side reading of the same interface behaviours the DSA bans; consent UI is where Apollo would meet it.

families.name: Deceptive design pattern taxonomy
families.quote: The user is drawn into a transaction on false pretences, because pertinent information is hidden
families.relevance: The negative space of the brain: a pattern library needs an anti-pattern list or it will happily generate Preselection.

families.name: Inclusive Design Principles
families.steward: Swan, Pouncey, Pickering, Watson (posters by Barclays Access)
families.licence: UNPROVEN: no licence statement in fetched text
families.quote: These Inclusive Design Principles are about putting people first
families.relevance: Bank-adjacent provenance (Barclays), and 'Be consistent' / 'Give control' collide productively with Apollo's four-theme flexibility rule.

families.name: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG)
families.quote: How to build accessibility semantics into web patterns and widgets
families.relevance: The behaviour contract #235 is chasing already exists in public for most widgets — APG is the natural external referent for a behaviour node.

families.name: Making Content Usable for People with Cognitive and Learning Disabilities
families.quote: Making Content Usable for People with Cognitive and Learning Disabilities W3C Working Group Note
families.relevance: The evidence-led answer to 'is this too complex?' — the cognitive-load question Apollo currently answers by eye.

families.name: Core Web Vitals / INP
families.licence: UNPROVEN: no licence statement captured (site is CC BY 4.0 by convention — NOT verified here)
families.quote: Interaction to Next Paint (INP) Optimize Interaction to Next Paint
families.relevance: The modern, measurable replacement for the folk Doherty 400 ms figure — and the number a dev will actually be held to.
families.caution: The 200 ms 'good' threshold did NOT appear in the fetched text (JS-rendered table). See UNPROVEN.

families.name: Android / Material touch-target guidance
families.quote: A touch target of 48x48dp results in a physical size of about 9mm
families.relevance: Gives Apollo's hit-area gate (s114-D3/D5, s116-D1) a second, physical-units rationale beside WCAG's 24 px.

families.name: Butterick's Practical Typography
families.licence: UNPROVEN: no licence statement in fetched text
families.quote: line length 45–90 characters or 2–3 alphabets
families.relevance: Directly contradicts the 45-75 figure the brief itself cites — a worked example of why fetching beats recalling.

families.name: Baymard Institute UX guidelines
families.quote: 200,000+ hours of UX research UX Best Practice Guidelines Over 700 UX Guidelines
families.relevance: The biggest e-commerce/checkout evidence base; paywalled, so it can be a POINTER in the graph, never a copied node.

families.name: Fogg Behavior Model (B=MAP)
families.steward: BJ Fogg / Stanford Behavior Design Lab
families.quote: three elements must converge at the same moment for a behavior to occur
families.relevance: The model behind onboarding and activation flows; sits one inch from the DSA Article 25 line and must be graded next to it.

families.name: Classic quantitative HCI models (Fitts, Hick, Hyman, Accot-Zhai, KLM)
families.quote: The information capacity of the human motor system in controlling the amplitude of movement
families.relevance: The only A-grade material in the whole survey. If the brain grades everything alike, these get diluted by 200 opinions.

families.name: Cognitive-psychology primaries (Miller, Cowan, Murdock, Sweller, Redelmeier-Kahneman)
families.quote: The magical number 4 in short-term memory: A reconsideration of mental storage capacity
families.relevance: Cowan is the correction Miller's 7±2 needs; Apollo's bento module counts must cite the correction, not the folk number.

families.name: Usability-method reliability literature (evaluator effect, CUE studies, sample size)
families.steward: Hertzum & Jacobsen; Molich & Dumas; Faulkner; Hornbaek
families.quote: The Evaluator Effect: A Chilling Fact About Usability Evaluation Methods
families.relevance: NEW FAMILY, not on the candidate list. It is the reason heuristics cap at grade C: two experts applying the same list disagree.

families.name: Information Foraging Theory
families.quote: Information foraging. Psychological Review (Pirolli, Card, 1999)
families.relevance: NEW FAMILY. Explains navigation/scent far better than the three-click rule it should replace in any brain Dave ships.

families.name: Cognitive Dimensions of Notations
families.quote: Usability Analysis of Visual Programming Environments: A 'Cognitive Dimensions' Framework
families.relevance: NEW FAMILY. A vocabulary for trade-offs (viscosity, premature commitment, hidden dependencies) — closer to Apollo's real problems than any 10-item list.

families.name: Situation awareness and multiple-resource workload models
families.quote: Toward a Theory of Situation Awareness in Dynamic Systems
families.relevance: NEW FAMILY. Dashboards are situation-awareness instruments; Apollo has bento dashboards and no theory of what they are FOR.

families.name: Technology Acceptance Model
families.quote: Perceived Usefulness, Perceived Ease of Use, and User Acceptance of Information Technology
families.relevance: NEW FAMILY. One of the most-replicated models in the field and completely absent from every designer's law list.

families.name: Graphical perception (dataviz encoding ranking)
families.quote: Graphical Perception: Theory, Experimentation, and Application to the Development of Graphical Methods
families.relevance: The empirical spine under Apollo's charts pillar; ranks position over angle over area — a testable claim, unlike 'Tufte says'.

families.name: RFC 9413 Maintaining Robust Protocols
families.quote: However, it has been interpreted in a variety of ways.
families.relevance: NEW FAMILY. The standards body that INVENTED Postel's Law formally walked it back — the cleanest 'a law can be demoted' receipt in the survey.

families.name: UIE / Center Centre empirical articles
families.quote: Hardly anybody gave up after three clicks.
families.relevance: The canonical worked example of a folk rule dying to data — the D grade needs a poster child and this is it.

families.name: Norman's principles (affordance, signifier, feedback, mapping, constraint)
families.licence: UNPROVEN: no licence statement in fetched text
families.quote: Social signifiers are those that are relevant to social usages
families.relevance: Norman corrected his own most-quoted term. The brain needs a field for 'the originator revised this' or it will ship the 1988 reading forever.
